910.name: Pre-Columbian El Salvador
910.description: Early Maya and Lenca settlement, Joya de Cerén volcanic preservation, and pre-Classic developments.

sub_clusters.name: Early Settlements and Chalchuapa
sub_clusters.description: Early village agriculture, pottery, Chalchuapa complex with Olmec-influenced jade trade.

sub_clusters.name: Joya de Cerén — Pompeii of the Americas
sub_clusters.description: Maya farming village buried by Loma Caldera eruption c. 600 CE, preserving daily life in extraordinary detail.

sub_clusters.name: Ilopango Eruption and Demographic Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Tierra Blanca Joven eruption (c. 431–540 CE), catastrophic depopulation of western El Salvador, refugee movements.

920.name: Pipil and Maya Post-Classic Heritage
920.description: Nahua-Pipil migration from central Mexico, Tazumal, Cihuatán, and Lenca territories at the time of conquest.

sub_clusters.name: Pipil (Nahua) Migration
sub_clusters.description: Nahua-speaking Pipil settle western El Salvador from central Mexico, bringing Toltec-influenced culture.

sub_clusters.name: Cihuatán and Tazumal
sub_clusters.description: Major post-Classic centres: Cihuatán's planned city, Tazumal's pyramids, ballcourts, feathered serpent motifs.

sub_clusters.name: Lenca Eastern Territories
sub_clusters.description: Lenca peoples in eastern highlands, independent chiefdoms, fierce resistance to Spanish conquest.

930.name: Spanish Conquest and Colonial Period
930.description: Alvarado's conquest, cacao and indigo export economies, colonial administration under the Captaincy General of Guatemala.

sub_clusters.name: Pedro de Alvarado's Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Spanish conquest, Battle of Acajutla, Atlacatl resistance (legendary), subjugation of Pipil and Lenca.

sub_clusters.name: Cacao and Indigo Export Economy
sub_clusters.description: Cacao boom and bust, transition to indigo as primary export, hacienda system, forced Indigenous labour.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial San Salvador
sub_clusters.description: San Salvador as provincial capital, Intendancy system (1786), Creole discontent, 1811 and 1814 uprisings.

940.name: Independence and Liberal-Conservative Struggles
940.description: Independence, Central American federation, caudillo politics, and transition to coffee monoculture.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Central American Federation
sub_clusters.description: Independence (1821), Mexican annexation, UPCA membership, federation collapse, sovereign republic.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of the Coffee Oligarchy
sub_clusters.description: Coffee replaces indigo, communal land expropriation, 'Fourteen Families' elite, rural proletariat created.

940.name: Coffee Republic and Authoritarian Rule
940.description: Military-oligarchic alliance, export dependence, indigenous marginalisation, and the 1932 Matanza.

sub_clusters.name: Military-Oligarchy Pact
sub_clusters.description: Coffee elite governs through military strongmen, labour repression, peasant dispossession.

sub_clusters.name: La Matanza (1932)
sub_clusters.description: Peasant-Indigenous uprising led by Farabundo Martí, brutal military massacre of 10,000-30,000, Indigenous cultural erasure.

950.name: Military Rule and Social Unrest
950.description: Decades of military governments, modernisation without democracy, Football War, growth of opposition.

sub_clusters.name: Successive Military Governments
sub_clusters.description: Hernández Martínez to subsequent juntas, limited reforms, industrialisation under CACM, repression.

sub_clusters.name: Football War (Soccer War)
sub_clusters.description: Brief war with Honduras triggered by migration tensions and World Cup qualifier, 3,000 casualties, CACM collapse.

sub_clusters.name: Growth of Revolutionary Opposition
sub_clusters.description: Death squads, land reform blocked, guerrilla groups form, Archbishop Romero's pastoral advocacy.

950.name: Salvadoran Civil War
950.description: 12-year civil war between military-government forces and FMLN guerrillas, 75,000 killed, US Cold War involvement.

sub_clusters.name: Archbishop Romero Assassination
sub_clusters.description: Óscar Romero murdered while celebrating Mass (24 March 1980), galvanises opposition, later canonised.

sub_clusters.name: FMLN Insurgency and US Intervention
sub_clusters.description: Five guerrilla groups unite as FMLN, US military aid exceeds $1M/day, Reagan Cold War proxy.

sub_clusters.name: El Mozote Massacre
sub_clusters.description: Atlacatl Battalion massacres ~1,000 civilians in Morazán, worst atrocity in modern Latin American history.

sub_clusters.name: Chapultepec Peace Accords
sub_clusters.description: UN-brokered peace, military reform, FMLN becomes political party, Truth Commission.

960.name: Post-War Democracy
960.description: ARENA and FMLN alternate in power, remittance economy, gang crisis, Mauricio Funes FMLN presidency.

sub_clusters.name: ARENA Governance Era
sub_clusters.description: Right-wing ARENA governs, neoliberal reforms, dollarization (2001), CAFTA, emigration surge.

sub_clusters.name: Gang Crisis (MS-13 and 18th Street)
sub_clusters.description: Deportees from LA bring MS-13/Barrio 18, extortion economy, world's highest homicide rates.

sub_clusters.name: FMLN in Government
sub_clusters.description: Funes and Sánchez Cerén presidencies, limited reform, corruption, continued violence.

960.name: Bukele and Nuevas Ideas
960.description: Nayib Bukele's disruptive presidency: state of exception, mass incarceration, Bitcoin legal tender, democratic erosion.

sub_clusters.name: Bukele Security Crackdown
sub_clusters.description: State of exception (March 2022), 80,000+ detained, gang power shattered, human rights concerns.

sub_clusters.name: Bitcoin as Legal Tender
sub_clusters.description: First country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender (Sep 2021), Chivo wallet, international criticism, volcano mining.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Erosion
sub_clusters.description: Supreme Court packing, legislative supermajority, re-election (2024), press freedom decline.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
